stations.name: Westlake
stations.description: Westlake station is the central hub of Link light rail, located beneath Westlake Center in downtown Seattle. It provides connections to the Seattle Center Monorail and numerous bus routes.

stations.name: Symphony
stations.description: Symphony station (formerly University Street) serves the downtown Seattle financial district, providing access to Benaroya Hall, numerous office buildings, and the Seattle Art Museum.

stations.name: Pioneer Square
stations.description: Pioneer Square station serves Seattle's historic Pioneer Square neighborhood, home to the original Seattle settlement and numerous art galleries.

stations.name: International District/Chinatown
stations.address: 5th Ave & S Jackson St, Seattle, WA 98104
stations.description: This station serves Seattle's International District and provides connections to Amtrak and Sounder commuter rail at King Street Station.

stations.name: Stadium
stations.address: 501 S Royal Brougham Way, Seattle, WA 98134
stations.description: Stadium station serves Lumen Field (Seahawks/Sounders) and T-Mobile Park (Mariners), making it a major destination for sporting events in Seattle.

stations.name: SODO
stations.description: SODO station serves Seattle's industrial SODO district, providing access to Starbucks headquarters and the busway with bus connections.

stations.name: Beacon Hill
stations.description: Beacon Hill station is located 160 feet underground in a deep-bore tunnel beneath Beacon Hill, making it one of the deepest stations in North America.

stations.name: Mount Baker
stations.description: Mount Baker station serves the Mount Baker neighborhood and provides major bus connections at the Mount Baker Transit Center.

stations.name: Columbia City
stations.address: S Edmunds St & 37th Ave S, Seattle, WA 98118
stations.description: Columbia City station serves the historic Columbia City neighborhood, known for its diverse dining, shops, and Rainier Valley Cultural Center.

stations.name: Othello
stations.address: Martin Luther King Jr Way S & S Othello St, Seattle, WA 98118
stations.description: Othello station serves the Othello neighborhood in the Rainier Valley, near New Holly mixed-income housing community.

stations.name: Rainier Beach
stations.description: Rainier Beach station serves the Rainier Beach neighborhood, the southernmost Seattle neighborhood on the Link line.

stations.name: Tukwila International Boulevard
stations.description: Tukwila International Boulevard station serves the city of Tukwila with a 600-stall park-and-ride and connections to King County Metro.

stations.name: SeaTac/Airport
stations.description: This station provides direct access to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, the largest airport in the Pacific Northwest.

stations.name: Angle Lake
stations.description: Angle Lake station is the current southern terminus of the 1 Line, featuring a 1,100-stall parking garage and named after nearby Angle Lake Park.

stations.name: Kent Des Moines
stations.address: Kent Des Moines Station, Kent, WA

stations.name: Star Lake
stations.address: Star Lake Station, Federal Way, WA

stations.name: Federal Way Downtown
stations.address: Federal Way Downtown Station, Federal Way, WA

stations.name: Capitol Hill
stations.description: Capitol Hill station serves one of Seattle's most vibrant neighborhoods, known for its nightlife, restaurants, and diverse community.

stations.name: University of Washington
stations.description: This station serves the University of Washington campus, one of the largest universities on the West Coast with over 50,000 students.

stations.name: U District
stations.description: U District station serves the University District neighborhood, located near the heart of the Ave (University Way NE) with its shops, restaurants, and proximity to the University of Washington.

stations.name: Roosevelt
stations.description: Roosevelt station serves the Roosevelt neighborhood in northeast Seattle, providing access to Green Lake and the surrounding residential areas.

stations.name: Northgate
stations.description: Northgate station is a major transit hub serving the Northgate neighborhood, with extensive park-and-ride facilities and bus connections.

stations.name: Shoreline South/148th
stations.description: Shoreline South/148th station serves the southern portion of Shoreline with a park-and-ride facility and bus connections.

stations.name: Shoreline North/185th
stations.description: Shoreline North/185th station serves northern Shoreline with a 500-stall park-and-ride garage and extensive bus connections.

stations.name: Mountlake Terrace
stations.description: Mountlake Terrace station serves the city of Mountlake Terrace with a major transit center and 1,200-stall park-and-ride garage.

stations.name: Lynnwood City Center
stations.description: Lynnwood City Center is the northern terminus of both the 1 Line and 2 Line, featuring a major transit center with 1,900-stall park-and-ride and connections to Community Transit and Sound Transit Express buses.

stations.name: Judkins Park
stations.description: Judkins Park station serves the Judkins Park and Atlantic neighborhoods, providing the 2 Line's entrance to the I-90 tunnel crossing Lake Washington.

stations.name: Mercer Island
stations.description: Mercer Island station is located in the center of I-90, serving the affluent island community with a park-and-ride and transit center.

stations.name: South Bellevue
stations.description: South Bellevue station features a 1,500-stall parking garage and serves as a major park-and-ride location for Eastside commuters.

stations.name: East Main
stations.description: East Main station serves the southeast edge of downtown Bellevue, near the Bellevue Club and Surrey Downs neighborhood.

stations.name: Bellevue Downtown
stations.description: Bellevue Downtown station serves the city center of Bellevue, the fifth largest city in Washington state and a major tech employment hub.

stations.name: Wilburton
stations.description: Wilburton station serves the Wilburton area including the Bellevue Botanical Garden and Spring District development.

stations.name: Spring District/120th
stations.description: Spring District/120th station serves the rapidly developing Spring District, home to Facebook/Meta's Bellevue campus and REI headquarters.

stations.name: Bel-Red/130th
stations.description: Bel-Red/130th station serves the Bel-Red corridor, an area transitioning from light industrial to mixed-use development.

stations.name: Overlake Village
stations.description: Overlake Village station serves the Overlake area and provides access to the Microsoft Connector shuttle system.

stations.name: Redmond Technology
stations.description: This station serves the Microsoft main campus and the broader Redmond tech corridor, home to numerous technology companies.

stations.name: Marymoor Village
stations.description: Marymoor Village station serves the Marymoor neighborhood adjacent to Marymoor Park, one of King County's largest parks, with a 200-stall park-and-ride.

stations.name: Downtown Redmond
stations.description: Downtown Redmond is the eastern terminus of the 2 Line, serving Redmond's city center with a transit center and 1,400-stall park-and-ride garage.

stations.name: Tacoma Dome
stations.description: Tacoma Dome station is the southern terminus of the T Line, connecting to Sounder commuter rail and regional bus services at the Tacoma Dome transit hub.

stations.name: Theater District
stations.description: Theater District station serves downtown Tacoma's cultural core, near the Tacoma Art Museum, Museum of Glass, and Washington State History Museum.

stations.name: Convention Center
stations.description: Convention Center station serves the Greater Tacoma Convention Center and is near the Tacoma Dome.

stations.name: Union Station
stations.description: Union Station serves Tacoma's historic Union Station (now a federal courthouse) and provides connections to Amtrak and Sounder commuter rail.

stations.name: S 25th Street
stations.address: S 25th St & Pacific Ave, Tacoma, WA 98402
stations.description: S 25th Street station serves the southern portion of downtown Tacoma near the University of Washington Tacoma campus.

stations.name: Stadium District
stations.address: N Stadium Way & N 1st St, Tacoma, WA 98403
stations.description: Stadium District station serves the Stadium District neighborhood, home to the historic Stadium High School and Stadium Bowl.

stations.name: S 4th
stations.address: S 4th St & Pacific Ave, Tacoma, WA 98402

stations.name: Old City Hall
stations.description: Old City Hall station is named for the nearby historic Tacoma Old City Hall, an 1893 Romanesque building.

stations.name: 6th Ave
stations.address: Division Ave & S 6th Ave, Tacoma, WA 98402
stations.description: Wright Park station serves Wright Park, a historic 27-acre urban park featuring the W.W. Seymour Botanical Conservatory.

stations.name: Tacoma General Hospital
stations.address: Martin Luther King Jr Way & S 5th St, Tacoma, WA 98405
stations.description: Tacoma General Hospital station provides access to MultiCare Tacoma General Hospital, one of the region's major medical centers.

stations.name: Hilltop District
stations.address: Martin Luther King Jr Way & S 1st St, Tacoma, WA 98405
stations.description: Hilltop District station is the western terminus of the T Line, serving Tacoma's historic Hilltop neighborhood.

stations.name: St Joseph
stations.address: Martin Luther King Jr Way & S Yakima Ave, Tacoma, WA 98405
stations.description: St Joseph station is the western terminus of the T Line's Hilltop extension, serving the Providence St. Joseph Medical Center area.
